citations.assessment: The Bavli names Chanina son of Yosi HaGelili as the permitting side of the slaughter dispute and Rabbi adjudicates the circumstances. The family and court roster does not occur in this segment.

The text explicitly distinguishes R. Yochanan ben Beroka on the first day from Chanina son of Yosi HaGelili on the second day. It confirms the father’s name here, irrespective of the preceding reference to his son Yishmael.
Both adjacent passages read Chananya son of Yosi HaGelili in the slaughter dispute.

The exact name Chananyah appears at Tosefta Hullin 2:2 in the found-animal case. This witness reverses the party labels in the initial ruling relative to the Bavli. The received chapter 12 does not correspond to the digital chapter.
The Usha prayer parallel names Chananyah son of Rabbi Yosi HaGelili; the digital locator is 6:8:10, with received halakhah 13 retained.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015

notes.text: The Bavli explicitly distinguishes the two Usha prayer leaders from the named son of Yochanan in the compiler’s roster. Three independently located parallels support the Chananyah variant. Retain the received Tosefta and Yerushalmi locator forms in the revised English.
